title: Dongwha Duty Free Shop
summary: Carries famous brands such as Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Bvlgari, Salvatore Ferragamo and Ermenegildo Zegna, and over 300,000 different imported goods are on display and sale.
overview:
Dongwha Duty Free Shop, opened in 1973, is the oldest duty-free shop in the heart of Seoul. The shop features around 250 of the world’s most famous brands such as Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Bvlgari, Salvatore Ferragamo and Ermenegildo Zegna, and over 300,000 different imported goods are on display and sale.

Dongwha Duty Free Shop is a convenient place for international tourists to enjoy sightseeing and shopping. It is within easy reach of the ancient palaces of Gyeongbokgung and Deoksugung (from the era of the Joseon Dynasty), and tourist attractions such as the Seoul Museum of Art and Cheonggyecheon (a stream running through Seoul and popular as a waterside walking route), making it the ideal place to enjoy both shopping and sightseeing at the same time.

The first floor features traditional Korean products including Korean ginseng, red ginseng, dried laver and kimchi (a traditional fermented Korean dish, made of vegetables with varied seasonings). In addition, there are various Korean cosmetics brands, and separate alpine clothing and jeans counters. They also carry wide variety of imported designer brands, such as Rolex, Omega, Gucci, Dior, Hermès and Celine, and is divided into different sections, such as a watches, sunglasses, bags, including LeSportsac and Furla, accessories & jewelry including Swarovski and Tateossian. However, visitors should note that there are no liquor or tobacco products in the shop.

Shinsegae, with a vision to respect and succeed the history and values of Korean aesthetics, meticulously restored the building’s original form, breathing new life into it as a unique cultural and shopping complex that encapsulates Korea’s advanced cultural standards together with history. overview:

In 1985 Dongdaemun Shopping Town was added to the complex bringing the total to four buildings altogether (A, B, C and Shopping Town). This traditional market houses many wholesale and retail stores specializing in various fabrics, materials, accessories, and wedding products. As much as eighty percent of all the fabric traded in Korea goes through here, allowing for goods to be sold at reasonable prices. Dongdaemun Shopping Complex first opened with over 5,000 shops crammed into three separate buildings. Recently the market was extensively refurbished and extended to include outlets selling quilts, corsages and handmade toys.

Since it was formed in 1994, the reputation of Mokdong Rodeo Street has as a fashion and cultural district has steadily grown. Situated in the middle of Mokdong apartment complex, Mokdong Rodeo Street is the originator of outlet stores, but has many features that are different from other outlets. First of all, clothing stores are grouped together by category into themed streets, for example, ladies’, men’s, casual and golf wear, rather than being scattered individually. Furthermore, as most stores are located on ground level, it is the perfect place for window-shopping as you take a stroll. overview:

The street began when shops selling off excess clothing stock opened here one by one. After walking about 500 meters from exit 1 of Munjeong Station, a cowboy statue first welcomes visitors. From here, the 2.5 kilometers of Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street begin, also known as the first fashion avenue. Both sides of the street are full with over 200 brand-name shops, making it easy to browse several famous brands at once. Always popular with shoppers are the 100 individual shops, as well as the multi-fashion malls such as Modes, Dump etc. or the outlet shops such as Cheil Industries Inc. and LG Fashion.

When you start to feel tired from shopping, Zelkova Park, situated just behind Munjeong-dong Office is the perfect place to take a rest. The park has a 600-year-old zelkova tree and provides refreshing rest areas. There are many restaurants, cafes, amusement arcades, food courts etc. located nearby, providing lots of interesting things to see, do and eat. As the nation's oldest outlet street, various festivals and cultural events are frequently held on Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street.

title: Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market
summary: Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market is famous for its “dokkaebi sale” held three times a week. The market sells various agricultural and marine products, including fruits and vegetables at low prices, attracting many shoppers.
overview:
Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market is famous for its “dokkaebi sale” held three times a week. The market sells various agricultural and marine products, including fruits and vegetables at low prices, attracting many shoppers. In particular, the market offers great value bargains in sales leading up to New Year's Day and Chuseok (Korean harvest festival). The market has 87 stores and 13 street vendors equipped with modern facilities, making it a convenient place to browse. The origin of the market dates back to 1982 when unlicensed street vendors began gathering here one by one, selling their goods in the evenings to avoid police patrols. Whenever officers came to the market to crack down, the vendors would disappear in an instant, earning the nickname, “dokkaebi”. Dokkaebi is a mythical being that appears in many old Korean folktales and is similar to a hobgoblin. During the early 2000s, the market faced crisis and risk of closure when a number of major discount supermarkets opened. In spite of this, since the market was renovated in 2004 it has grown to become one of the busiest traditional markets.

Many items in Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market are priced 30 to 40 percent cheaper than in the major supermarkets. In the middle of the market, displays of the most popular items can be found in every shop at 20 to 30 percent cheaper. The market also holds huge bargain sales before the festive seasons. Traditional Korean banchan (side dishes) can be purchased at very reasonable prices in Banchan stores. It is very common to see overseas visitors in the market buying different types of banchan. These include Kimchi and Tteok, traditional Korean cakes. The market also has sections for fruit and vegetables, seafood and meat. Cosmetics and confectionery are also sold in the market at cheap prices. Seafood and meat are delivered directly from their place of origin, so customers can be sure they are buying fresh produce.

title: Cheonggyecheon Secondhand Book Street
summary: Many visitors trek from afar in order to search for limited editions and rare books, nostalgic of the smell of ink and the increasingly rare sight of books piled from floor to ceiling, wall to wall.
overview:
Book Street at the Peace Market

When you hear "Dongdaemun" you may immediately think of the Doosan Tower and the Migliore Fashion Mall, or you may not. Upon close inspection, Dongdaemun is easily one of the most difficult places to categorize in Seoul. New shopping alleys are spawning around the vicinity, alley to street, street to alley. The Cheonggyecheon Peace Market's Secondhand Book Street is one of these hidden jewels. Growing steadily since the 1960s, many collectioners trek from afar in order to search for limited editions and rare books, nostalgic of the smell of ink and the increasingly rare sight of books piled from floor to ceiling, wall to wall.

One Man's Trash is Another's Treasure
Living history seems to seep out of these books that can be found here. Limited editions of Korean masterpieces, hard to find foreign comics and magazines, and even stores specializing in design and home interiors can be found here. Some of the stores are so small and so full of books that you will most likely be shoulder-to-shoulder with other bibliophiles searching for lost treasures. You could easily spend hours just looking at titles here until an entire day has gone by. In general, prices for books cost 30% lower than elsewhere. Of course, price will also depend on the condition and the rarity of the item you are seeking to purchase.

They offer a wide range of luxurious hanboks in subtle pastel colors, as well as a variety of accessories, so you can try on different styles and find the one that suits you best. Many people are looking for luxury hanboks for weddings and other important family events.

title: FilmLog
summary: Film Developing Studio Located at Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station
overview: Located at Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station, FilmLog is a film developing studio dedicated to preserving the value of film in today's era. They play a crucial role in spreading film culture and engage in various activities related to film without limiting their services. The studio focuses on key operations such as film developing, scanning, printing, selling films and cameras, exhibitions, and film camera repairs. Additionally, they offer workshops, classes, and support programs for those who wish to share and learn about film culture. FilmLog also features a film camera vending machine, making it easy for anyone to experience film photography. The staff are always present to provide friendly explanations, so even first-time visitors can use their services without any worries.

The GENTLE MONSTER store inside runs pop-ups that show off the brand's talent for building a space. Come expecting an exhibition as much as a shop.

title: GROVE
summary: A popular fashion brand in Korea
overview:
Established in 2020, GROVE blends 1960s retro style with casual fashion, presenting a brand identity that is both classic and understated.
The brand has received positive attention after being worn by many artists and influencers, including members of NewJeans, aespa, and actress Han So-hee, in their personal styling. Within just a few years, GROVE has gained significant popularity among Korean women in their 20s and 30s.
A visit to GROVE offers a glimpse into the recent fashion trends that have defined Korean women’s style in the past few years.

title: GS25 DX LAB Store
summary: A next-generation futuristic convenience store with DX LAB & CAFÉ
overview: GS25 DX LAB & CAFE is GS25’s premium convenience store that also serves as a café. It offers a variety of unique products not found in other branches, providing the joy of discovery. Café services are self-operated through a SELF ZONE, and the store operates unmanned from midnight to 6 a.m. Guests can also experience advanced systems such as kiosks recommending whiskey and wine, self-checkout counters, AI smart vending machines, and facial recognition payment.

title: Gaemi Supermarket

overview: Opened in the 1900s, Gaemi Super has a history with the surrounding sewing industry. There were many sewing shops leading from Seoul Station to Namdaemun Market. The employees of the sewing shops were the customers of the store, but in the 2000s, the sewing industry became specialized and the store's sales plummeted. However, in 2015, foreigners started coming to the area, and they started taking pictures with them, and it became a culture. As a testament to this, one wall of Gaemi Super is covered with photos of foreign customers and the owner.

title: Gajungsic Fabric

overview: Gajungsic Fabric is a clothing brand showroom in Shina Memorial Hall on Jeongdong-gil. The brand aims to create natural and comfortable clothing using materials close to nature. In this cozy space, you can explore clothing that harmonizes with the natural world. Seasonal exhibitions frequently feature various works, from glass crafts to embroidery, rattan crafts, and felt crafts, offering themes not commonly seen in daily life. You can observe Junmyeongjeon Hall from the windows as it changes with the seasons. It is a serene spot where you can take a break from your walk along Jeongdong-gil, browse the clothing, and relax.

title: Garden Beau
summary: A duty-free beauty store near Seoul Botanic Park
overview:
Garden Beau , inspired by “Gardens by the Bay” in Singapore, is a beauty, health, and organic specialty store located near Seoul Botanic Park. It is a multi-store where visitors can experience a wide range of products across various categories, featuring both domestic and international brands, making it a beloved destination.

The store offers Global Tax-Free services and multilingual assistance (English, Japanese, Chinese). Various ongoing events are provided for foreign visitors, making it especially popular among tourists.
subway: Subway Line 9, Yangcheon Hyanggyo Station, Exit 8, 467m

title: Gawon Craft Studio
summary: A workshop run by a jade crafter (Seoul Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 37)
overview: Run by Seoul Intangible Cultural Property Okjang Uhm Ik-pyeong, Gawon Gongbang is a place where you can see artisan artworks made of jade. Mr. Uhm has been practicing jade crafts for 47 years, starting in 1974. Gawon Gongbang is a family-run exhibition hall and store where you can see Okjang's jade artwork, Korean traditional jewelry made from various materials such as jade, coral, and milhua, and a variety of jewelry with traditional and modern designs.

title: Gembros Gioro Jewelry
summary: A renowned jewelry establishment that pioneered the Korean jewelry industry
overview:
The House of GEMBROS: The House that Designs Light

Since 1984, GEMBROS has been a fine & wedding jewelry house that completes the entire process under one roof, from grading and design to craftsmanship and lifetime care, based on natural diamonds, colored gemstones, and pearls carefully selected directly from origins and mines around the world.

Over 5,000 product archives and a cumulative 10,000+ design archives accumulated since 1984 represent the density of time GEMBROS has walked, and serve as the foundation that has further refined its origin-first philosophy of deeply observing the source, texture, and light properties of gemstones. Upon this accumulation, the house's aesthetics of naturalistic design, natural stone gradation, and organic curve crafting are added along with the touch of 60-year artisans and precise standards to complete a single masterpiece that most persuasively reveals the essential beauty and brilliance of each gemstone.

GEMBROS does not stop at merely creating beautiful jewelry; it takes responsibility for the entire lifespan of the artwork—from the selection and recording of gemstones, stone-centric design, and precise handcrafting, to aftercare that protects its value over time. Centered around the Gangnam Atelier, it organically connects the grading room, design studio, crafting room, and exhibition space to realize high perfection and transparency, and designs light so that today's choice becomes tomorrow's legacy through the Stone Passport and lifetime care.

overview: Established in Korea in 2011, Gentle Monster is a fashion eyewear brand. summary: Gentle Monster's flagship store, located in Hongdae, Seoul.
overview: Gentle Monster's flagship store, "SACRIFICE," located in Hongdae, Seoul, tells the story about the god of the earth and the ceremony to honor him. Gentle Monster Hongdae consists of three floors, and visitors can find colorful sunglasses and glasses along with various exhibits. In particular, in the garden on the first floor, visitors can see a statue dedicated to the "Eye of God." Take a picture or two at Gentle Monster in Hongdae with its unique and sophisticated look.

title: Gentle Monster Sinsa Flagship Store
summary: Gentle Monster is Korea’s eyewear brand, which has been a viral sensation through collaborations with K-Wave celebrities. Gentle Monster’s flagship store, which is located in Sinsa District’s boulevard.
overview: Gentle Monster is a domestic eyewear brand that has garnered attention through collaborations with popular Hallyu stars. The Gentle Monster Sinsa flagship store in Garosu-gil, Sinsa-dong, features a striking white exterior, a large entrance, and an open first-floor layout that catches the eye. The biggest attraction of Gentle Monster is its unique approach of varying the concept and design of each location, offering diverse interiors and spatial changes. The Sinsa flagship store is no exception.Renovated in June 2023, this place features the theme 'TIME - SLEEP,' presenting an imaginative story that creates a time-slip phenomenon through the medium of sleep. The fantasy of time slips is expressed through large art objects, with research into structural forms and the movements of animals resulting in extraordinary scenes. Each floor showcases a variety of eyeglass collections and objects with unique designs, creating a stylish and distinctive space. Inspired by the movements and forms of living creatures, the artfully expressed objects invite visitors to escape reality and experience their own fantasies.

title: Geulbeot Books
address: 210 World Cup buk-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea
summary: A secondhand bookstore with rare first copies of literary classics
overview: Geulbeot Books started as a used bookstore called Ongodang, which the owners inherited from their maternal uncle in 1979. It had a reputation as a bookstore specializing in art in front of Hongdae University. Today, the store sells a wide variety of books other than art books, and many of its longtime customers come in and ask if they can help them find a book. The slogan "All the books in the world are people" is written in large letters on the outside wall of the building, and he wanted to convey the truth that only people can read books. title: Geulwoll Yeonhui Branch
summary: A Place Offering Letter-Related Products and Services
overview: "Glewol," a pure Korean word meaning 'letter,' is also used to honor the act of writing letters. Since 2019, Glewol has operated a letter shop in Seoul, offering a variety of letter-related products and services. The store aims to make letter writing a part of modern culture, continuing the value and spirit of writing letters. At the Glewol Yeonhui branch, you can experience a penpal service for a fee of 10,000 KRW, where you can exchange replies with someone you don't know. The cozy space is filled with various items such as stationery, postcards, and fountain pens. There is also a designated area where you can sit and write letters after purchasing your stationery, allowing you to enjoy the ambiance of Glewol while crafting your letters.

overview: The owner, a 40-year veteran, makes name tags with personalized wording. A small signboard with dents and peeling paint shows the shop's age. The sign that reads "Name tags, zakk, buttons" is also nostalgic. The owner is a master of the art of "snabari," which involves embroidering name tags and patching holes in clothes with small patterns. overview: Geunyeong Musical Instruments is a specialized instrument shop located in Nakwon Arcade in Jongno, Seoul, led by a veteran performer who has worked in Nakwon Arcade since 1995. Based on extensive field experience, the shop provides practical consultations and sales of wind and string instruments including flutes, tailored to the performance level and budget of beginners through professionals. title: Ginger House

overview: Ginger House serves as the showroom for Ginger Eyewear, a Seoul-based brand known for creating naturally harmonious glasses that prioritize comfort. As visitors step inside, they are welcomed by Ginger House's signature fragrance and an interior that enhances the display of the glasses. The showroom provides personalized assistance to help guests find the ideal pair of glasses while offering special touches like uniquely designed cases that embody Ginger Eyewear's distinctive aesthetic. Additionally, workshops and pop-up events are frequently hosted, making checking the website for updates worthwhile.

summary: A bookstore that sparked an uprising of Seoul National University students
overview: 'Gnal’ is the center of Seoul National University's student culture and the last remaining bookstore specializing in humanities and social sciences in Korea. It supported the student movement as the spiritual root and center of the student movement in the 1980s. As a result, the owner was once detained for selling transfer marks under the National Security Act, but he was released after fierce student protests. The name 'Gnal’ is derived from a poem by Shim Hoon, and reflects the president's belief in contributing to a better world in the 1980s, when Korean society was eager to change.

title: Goyoseosa

overview: Nestled in Haebangchon, beneath Namsan Mountain, this tiny bookstore opened its doors in the fall of 2015. It aspires to be a "literature-focused bookstore," with shelves primarily filled with novels, poetry, and essays. The bookstore also curates humanities, social sciences, and art books related to themes often explored in literature, such as human rights, gender, historical events, and alternative lifestyles, offering readers a rich and varied selection. The bookstore is dedicated to selecting books with strong readability, excellent prose, and harmonious design and layout. It also hosts book talks, readings, and ongoing workshops on reading and writing while planning and conducting new types of book-related events.

title: Granhand : Dosan Branch
summary: A trendy Korean fragrance brand created entirely in-house
overview:
Granhand, a Korean fragrance brand established in 2014, has continued to uphold its brand philosophy of being unpretentious, emotional, and warm. The brand does not run advertisements, does not use celebrities as models, and even its packaging remains modest.

The label on each bottle gives the impression of being handmade, emphasizing Granhand’s pursuit of a brand style that stays close to everyday life.

If you are purchasing a fragrance as a gift, Granhand offers a label engraving service at its stores. You can print a personalized message on the bottle label, making it a thoughtful and customized present for a loved one or friend.

title: Gukseon Otchil
summary: Since 1977, this place has been selling lacquerware inlaid with mother-of-pearl.
overview:
This store has been selling lacquerware since 1977. The store has a history of 40 years and is run by two generations. The first-generation owner came to Seoul alone when he was 19 years old and learned the craft for the first time at a lacquer workshop that solves room and board. Located in Gwangjang Market, the project was acquired by his son, a cultural asset function, under the new name of national lacquer. Today, the business exports mother-of-pearl products to countries around the world and has developed its reputation as a traditional craft shop representing Korean style.

Now in its third generation, Gwangseong Distribution continues to offer fresh nuts daily, incorporating decades of expertise. With a transparent pricing policy, anyone can comfortably enjoy the high-quality nuts from Gwangseong Distribution.

title: HONGIKMUNGO
summary: A popular hangout in Sinchon and Seoul's oldest bookstore
overview:
Hongik Books started as a street vendor in 1957 and has become a Sinchon landmark for over 60 years, making it South Korea's oldest bookstore. It was once a popular meeting spot in Sinchon. The bookstore moved to its current building in 1978, initially using only the first and second floors, and expanded to occupy the entire building in 1984. Now in its second generation of family operation, Hongik Books takes its name from the Hongik Ingan philosophy, which means "to benefit humanity broadly." The bookstore is dedicated to serving customers, partners, employees, and family. In front of Hongik Books is "Literary Street," which features the handprints of 15 prominent Korean writers and hosts romantic street piano concerts.

The current owner worked as a tailor for 30 years before taking over the business. Countless politicians have visited the shop, including the late President Kim Dae-jung and foreign prime ministers. overview:
Haechang Tailor shop is Sogong-dong’s oldest tailor shop with over 90 years of history. Having started its origin in Bosu-dong, Busan back in 1929, it moved locations to Sogong-dong, Seoul in 1945 and developed an impressive list of clientele including many historical figures in Korea.

Haechang Tailor Shop was a beloved shop of many prominent political figures in Korean history. This shop was able continue to maintain business due to their high quality service and suits. Through constant communication with their customers, the shop make suits that accurately reflect the individual customer's style through details. One of Korea's first tailor shop, many students who used to learn and work in this store has set up their own tailor shops throughout Korea.

title: Hansin Pottery
summary: A pottery that has been running in Haebangchon for 50 years
overview:
Hanshin Ongi is a pottery and ceramics shop that has been protecting Liberation Village for 50 years. Once you step inside, you'll be spoiled for choice with a wide range of useful products, including jars, pottery, and teacups, as well as interior accessories. The clay pots on display at Hanshin Ongi are all handmade in Icheon, a city famous for its ceramics. The 50-meter long procession of clay pots lining the exterior wall is Hanshin Ongi's signature photo zone, evoking nostalgic memories for locals and unique Korean feelings for foreigners.

Visit Hapdeok Super, which has been transformed from a living space into a retro attraction, to take photos and taste the cool drinks and sweets sold at the store.

title: Hetras Seongsu
summary: A lifestyle shop enveloped in scents.

Located in the central area of Seongsu, the four-story building is filled with fragrant spaces, and you can directly test various products. Furthermore, you can experience an art space rather than simple shopping.

Hoehyeon Secondhand LP Arcade has nestled in an underground shopping center in Hoehyeon-dong since 1980s, and mainly deals in LPs (long-playing records) which have been discontinued. After reorganization of the shopping center in 2003, the number of the LP stores dwindled to just a handful. However, since domestic production for LPs stopped in 2004, this arcade has become a popular place with LP enthusiasts.

Hoehyeon Secondhand LP Arcade is situated in Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center in the basement of Shinsegae Department Store; stores in the arcade stock secondhand CDs as well as LPs. Outside the stores, boxes are stacked with what appears at a glance to be thousands of LPs and CDs. Many of the record jackets are well-thumbed, reminding us how much history the albums contain. title: Itaewon Books

overview:

It was founded in 1967 by a U.S. military unit that collected and delivered used books to bookstores and operated a stall with leftover books. At the time, foreign books were rare, especially those in color. A few years later, in 1973, he opened his own bookstore, where he has remained for over 40 years. It mainly deals with used books in English and American languages, and its categories are as diverse as a large bookstore, including poetry, fiction, philosophy, psychology, travel, religion, dictionaries, and history.

He went through all the famous handmade shoe alleys in Seoul, and even went to France and Italy to study shoe making. title: Jackson Chameleon

overview:
Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street, located in Jongno, a central district of Seoul, is well known nationwide. It is estimated to house between 2,000 and 4,000 jewelry stores of every size and packed close together in one district. Jongno district has always had a large floating population and has been a well-developed commercial area since olden times. The jewelry street in its current form has existed since the 1960s. Even though the area has repeatedly undergone major changes to its academic and entertainment venues, the jewelry street continues to be as lively as ever. At present, about 70 percent of the domestic jewelry market is traded on Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street.

The first thing that catches the eye is the number of wholesale and retail stores lining the street (Jongnodaero), which now form a new commercial zone in the area. Here, customers can purchase jewelry at around 20 to 40 percent cheaper than market prices, since most stores have close connections with jewelry-makers and can lower prices. Proof of this is the number of gold-and-silver workshops nearby, in an area slightly bigger than 3.3 square meters. Jewelry Street is especially popular with lovers and soon-to-be-married couples, and overseas tourists frequently visit looking for Korean jewelry at low prices.

title: Namdaemun Galchi-jorim(Hairtail) Alley
summary: The Galchi-jorim Alley inside Namdaemun Market
overview:
Namdaemun Market's Braised Hairtail Alley was formed around 1988. It became famous through word of mouth as hairtail, which was inexpensive at the time, was braised into a deliciously spicy and savory dish tailored to the tastes of the local merchants.
Braised hairtail was not the signature menu of the Namdaemun Market Braised Hairtail Alley from the very beginning. The restaurants originally sold dishes like kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and dumplings before switching to fish dishes, selling braised hairtail alongside braised mackerel and braised pollack. Braised hairtail became exceptionally popular, attracting not only market workers but also nearby office employees, which began to draw in large crowds of customers. Today, it is a destination frequently visited by many Japanese tourists as well.
Although the origin of the hairtail varies slightly by restaurant, they use domestic hairtail sourced directly from Yeosu, Mokpo, Busan, and Jeju. Because each shop has a different cooking method, you can enjoy uniquely different flavors at each place. If you find spicy food a bit challenging, we highly recommend visiting a restaurant that also serves grilled fish!

Seongsu Yeonmujang-gil is a multi-cultural street located in Seongdong-gu, Seoul, a space where industrial traces of former shoe factories blend with modern sensibility. The name 'Yeonmujang' originates from where soldiers practiced martial arts during the Joseon Dynasty. It has become a sanctuary for the Millennials, Gen Z, and creators, featuring the cultural complex 'Daelim Warehouse' converted from a red brick warehouse to stylish cafes, galleries, clothing boutiques, and various brand pop-up stores.
It's a popular destination for those wanting to experience Seongsu's unique atmosphere, especially with the Dior Seongsu, which has established itself as a splendid photo zone, and consecutive pop-up stores from global brands.
subway: 533m from Seongsu Station, Subway Line 2, Exit 3

title: Seongwoo Barbershop
summary: A barbershop that has kept its place for over a century
overview:
Seongwoo Barbershop is the oldest barbershop in Seoul, opened around 1927 and passed down through three generations of the family. It has remained in the same location for nearly 100 years and still retains its traditional culture. They pride themselves on using only scissors and combs to give each customer a haircut that best suits their head and face shape. Seongwoo Barbershop was transformed into its current form through a project supported by the Seoul Metropolitan Government to prevent the loss and damage of Seoul's future heritage after the building collapsed due to a typhoon in 2019.

title: Seonyudo Cat
summary: A cat-themed variety shop that cat lovers cannot simply walk past
overview: Seonyudo Cat is a space that collects stories of cats from around the world. Located in Seonyudo, a place known for cat-related legends, it holds a unique connection to the area’s past. In the old days, there was a peak on Seonyudo called Seonyubong, whose shape resembled a cat, and it was nicknamed "Gwaengi Mountain" (Cat Mountain). Here, you can discover cat-related goods sourced from around the globe, as well as cleverly designed pieces by creative artists.

Through regular entry evaluations, the store continues to expand the range of product entries and support. It promotes coexistence with local regions through a variety of online activities, including its online shopping mall, and offline activities through the store.

overview: This record store has been in operation since 1976 and offers a wide range of LP, CD, and cassette tapes. When you enter the store, you'll feel like you're in an old-fashioned museum. Many record stores are located in the basement, but Seoul Record is on the first floor, making it easy to access. Inside the store, you'll find a wide variety of music for all ages.

title: Soil Baker Jeongdong-gil
address: Shina Memorial Hall, Room 202, 33 Jeongdong-gil, Jung-gu, Seoul
summary: A quiet crockery shop located in Jeongdong Shina Memorial Hall
overview: Soil Baker, which means "a person who bakes soil," is a tableware brand on the second floor of the red-brick Shina Memorial Hall on Jeongdong-gil. It showcases various interpretations of tableware by ceramists, designers, and chefs. The spacious area displays a wide variety of tableware, allowing visitors to browse comfortably. The dishes are highlighted on tables and shelves made from various materials and colors, such as glass, wood, and ceramics—the arrangement of the tableware changes with the seasons, adding a touch of detail. The quiet and serene atmosphere, combined with views of Deoksugung's Jungmyeongjeon Hall and Jeongdong-gil through the windows, provides comfort.
subway: Subway Lines 1/ 2 City Hall Station Exit 12, 507m

title: Songlim
summary: A store run by a shoemaker who produces the most comfortable handcrafted shoes
overview:
The sound of hammers began in a small workshop on Euljiro 3-ga in 1936 to make the world's only shoes and the most comfortable shoes. With 80 years of hard-earned know-how, Songlim Sujehwa pays attention to every detail, starting with measuring the exact shape of each customer's foot. To create a comfortable shoe, the company not only relies on excellent craftsmanship, but also on the finest materials. For this reason, politicians, mountain climbers, business representatives, and other customers who are looking for good shoes often visit.

Middle-aged actors who have been coming here since their younger days often stop by to say hello to Hwang Soo-yeon. Yeouido office workers who want to have their portraits taken are also frequent visitors.

Specializing in independent and small-scale publications, this independent bookstore is just a 5-minute walk from its sister branch. The shop features various books across genres you won't typically find in mainstream bookstores. The walls are adorned with thoughtfully curated book-related goods, making it a perfect spot for leisurely browsing. Storage Book & Film has been a cherished neighborhood staple for years and is loved by many. Books can be ordered online, with international shipping available. Additionally, their Instagram account features introductions to newly stocked books and updates on various programs hosted by Storage Book & Film, so don't forget to check it out.

From 2013 to 2019, it created and managed the independent publication fair "Publishers Table," and currently, it hosts, organizes, and manages the "Little Press Fair." Since 2016, it has been co-hosting and managing a podcast called "Small Pocket" with author Taejae. It shares and discusses the stories of independent publishers, bookstore operators, and small brand owners. Along with running the bookstore, various programs are managed through Club Storage.

title: Stylenanda

The cozy shop space, which complements Mangwon-dong's local sensibility, is charmingly decorated, offering the fun of browsing and simple delight.

The building's interior is based off of a lantern-inspired motif, following a philosophy that represents the brand's commitment to illuminate beauty. The Sulwhasoo flagship store, which has years of beauty experience and wisdom, is a space where visitors can experience eternal beauty. On the first floor of the building, visitors can see the history of the brand, which started in 1996, and they can test and purchase a variety of Sulwhasoo products. overview: Located in Insadong since 1984, Talbang offers a wide variety of traditional handmade masks. In the show window, you can see the hahoe, which symbolizes the Korean face, as well as gakshi, yangban used in snadae nori. The workshop uses wood to restore traditional Korean masks, and all the pieces are handmade. The process of making a hahoe-tal is also on display. Although it is a small store of about 4 square meters, the owner of Talbang has been working on various creative works here.

title: The Book Society

overview: The Book Society is a Seoul-based collective that has published editorial work under Mediabus since 2010. It plans exhibitions and projects. Additionally, it operates a bookstore and project space called The Book Society, where it sells and distributes domestic and international books related to contemporary art and design. You can follow its events and updates through its blog and social media platforms, including Instagram, Facebook, and X.

title: Tongmungwan
summary: The Korea’s oldest bookstore with national treasure-level cultural artifacts
overview:
Tongmungwan is an old bookstore that opened in 1934, and has been opening for three generations. It is a bookstore that discovers, evaluates, analyzes, distributes, and publishes ancient Korean books, and has discovered numerous cultural assets such as "Wolin Seokbo" and "Independent Newspaper." It is currently run by Lee Jong-un, the grandson of founder and first director Lee Geom-ro. The main customers are those who study and study ancient books, collectors who invest in the value of ancient books, and Japanese and Chinese tourists who are familiar with Chinese characters, according to the commission.

The bookstore is filled with cozy spots where you can linger and enjoy your time. In this space brimming with imagination, it’s okay to lose your way and explore freely with your own interpretations. Without being confined to predefined structures, you can discover new perspectives here. Welcome to Yeonnam-dong UHJJUHDAH Book Shop, where you’re invited to read each other anew.

title: VILLA ERBATIUM
summary: A Korean niche perfume brand that captures the scent of Seoul’s unique mood.
overview: Villa Ervatium is a Korean niche perfume brand often referred to as an “emotional perfume” for its aim to evoke feelings at the boundary of science and art. The name combines Villa (Italian for cultural space), Erva (Italian for herb), and Tium (a native Korean noun form of “to sprout”), reflecting the brand’s belief that “what comes from nature is best for people.” All fragrances use natural ingredients extracted from flowers, leaves, stems, and roots. In the brand’s classically styled store, customers can test various scents while enjoying curated videos, music, and visuals that turn the olfactory experience into a multisensory one.

title: Vintage Shop Page-One

The first floor features women’s vintage clothing and small goods, while the second floor offers brand-name vintage and imported selected items. Shoppers can find products from Australia, Europe, the United States, Japan, and other countries.

title: Vintage Universe

overview: Take Exit 10 of Euljiro 3-ga Station and you'll see a sign that says 'Dojang'. If you enter the alley with the sign, you'll find a shop called Yemoonsa. As the sign in front of the shop says, "Best technology, low price," the owner of Yemoonsa has been handwriting and selling seal for 50 years without using printing or machines. Since the advent of stamping machines, handmade stamp shops have largely closed down, unable to keep up with the times. Yemoonsa's shop has been operating steadily by combining four businesses: writing, keys, seal and stationery.

There is a powder room where you can apply makeup and do your hair before your photo shoot, and they have a wide selection of headbands and hair accessories. title: buruttrak
summary: A record shop opened in Myeong-dong in 1979.
overview: Buruttrak, established in 1978, is a long-standing record shop still in operation today. Known as a landmark in Myeong-dong, it has appeared in films and dramas several times. The first floor features K-pop albums and merchandise, the second floor sells jazz and pop CDs, and the third and fourth floors are dedicated to classical vinyl records. Within the vast collection of over 100,000 records, there is a particularly large selection of classical LPs. With some luck, you might also find rare albums by American Black musicians from the 1980s and 1990s. In the 1990s, as the hobbies of the Korean public shifted, record purchases began to decline. However, Japanese LP enthusiasts started buying records at high prices. During this period, the main customer base gradually shifted to foreigners. By the late 1990s, Korean record shops became essential tourist spots for Japanese visitors who could buy K-albums cheaper than in their country. Back then, the area around Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center and Myeong-dong had 11 record shops, with 'Buruttrak' being a well-established figure. Nowadays, with K-pop's global popularity, the shop attracts customers from Southeast Asia and Europe, and it stocks a wide variety of records to meet diverse tastes.

title: Daerim Jungang Market

overview: Appearing as a setting for the movie “The Outlaws,” Daerim Jungang Market is well known Chinatown inside Seoul. Although it appeared as a dangerous and shady place in the movie, the actual atmosphere of this place is much brighter and friendlier. Walking through this market amidst the street vendors selling dumplings, Yeonbeon (sausage) sundae, and many other exotic Chinese food will make you feel as if you took a short trip to China.

title: Dongdaemun Market
summary: Dongdaemun Market is a large commercial district comprised of traditional markets and shopping centers that covers the entire area around Dongdaemun Gate, a prominent landmark in Korea.
overview:
Dongdaemun Market is a large commercial district comprised of traditional markets and shopping centers that covers the entire area around Dongdaemun Gate, a prominent landmark in Korea. It is Korea’s largest wholesale and retail shopping district, featuring 26 shopping malls, 30,000 speciality shops, and 50,000 manufacturers. All kinds of goods can be found here including silks and fabric, clothes, shoes and accessories, electronics, leather goods, sporting goods, office supplies, pet products, and toys.

Although Dongdaemun Market is traditionally famous for its night market, this popular shopping district attracts hordes of shoppers and tourists at all times of day. Like Namdaemun Market, Dongdaemun Market sells a variety of products, but unlike Namdaemun Market, it is open 24-hours a day. The powerful appeal of Dongdaemun Market stems from the fact that you can buy everything you need at a reasonable price, in one convenient location and at anytime. Most major wholesalers and retailers are here along with specialist outlets focusing on the youth market, making Dongdaemun Market the best place to find the latest fashions at bargain prices. Dongdaemun’s famous food alley, Mukja Golmok, is also essential for anyone wanting to check out the latest trends in Korean cuisine.

In addition to selling everything under the sun, large shopping malls such as Good Morning City and Freya add an extra dimension to the shopping experience with their own multiplex cinemas, while Doota features a huge outdoor concert hall hosting a range of events including outdoor fashion shows, concerts, modeling contests and classical Korean music for tourists.

title: Dongmyo Flea Market
summary: Dongmyo Flea Flea Market started life in the late 1980s.
overview:
Dongmyo Flea Market started life in the late 1980s. Every day an array of street stalls open up along the stone walls of Dongmyo Park. The main items bought and sold here are antiques of every type, including items such as wallets, electronics, old books, film posters etc. Recently vintage clothing and shoes have become the main area of interest. Prices are typically around 1,000 won so you can have fun browsing and shopping without worrying about the cost.

There are all kinds of items from everyday miscellaneous goods to antiques. If you get peckish while shopping, boiled duck's eggs cost just 1,500 won each or bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) make very satisfying snacks. The market is always crowded with people at weekends. The most popular item in Dongmyo Flea Market is used clothing. When new stocks arrive, the market is packed with people looking for bargains. Prices are normally around 1,000 won, but leather items or furs reach around 10,000 won. Designer labels can reach over 100,000 won. The best time for shopping is on weekend afternoons.

title: Dongnimmun Yeongcheon Market
summary: Dongnimmun Yeongcheon Market not only sells a wide range of produce and ingredients from fruits to seafood, but also sells stationery and secondhand books.
overview: Dongnimmun Yeongcheon Market, located between Seodaemun Station and Dongnimmun Station, started as a tteok (Rice Cake) alley near Seodaemun Prison in the 1960s. With its unique and diverse streets filled with kkwabaegi (Twisted Bread Stick,) tteok-bokki (Stir-fried Rice Cake,) meat, fish, vegetables, and fruits, words have spread on social media and this market has become trendy among young people.

title: Garak Mall

overview: Garak Mall, formerly known as Garak Market, is a huge modernized market offering a wide range of agricultural products and experience. Selling fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, dairy, seafood, and kitchen products in its "Sale Zone" and offering various experience programs about Korean food in its 5 different "Theme Zone", Garak Mall also has available a library, cooking studio, convention center, restaurants, hospital, bank, and more under its “Task Zone”, offering visitors a new kind of convenient shopping experience.

overview: Geumnam Market has existed in Geumho-dong since before the Korean War. title: Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market
summary: Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors gathered near Hwarangdae
overview: The Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors who gathered near Hwarangdae Station when the Gyeongchun Railway opened on July 25, 1939. Named for its fleeting nature, like a goblin's visit, the vendors would quickly disappear at the sign of a crackdown and reassemble snugly along the tracks to rebuild the market once things were clear. This traditional goblin market is the precursor to today's Gongneung-dong Goblin Market. Since then, the market has operated as a quintessential neighborhood market in Nowon-gu, as if a goblin's magic wand has made every possible item available. It offers a variety of products including livestock, groceries, restaurants, miscellaneous goods, and agricultural products. The market draws a steady stream of visitors due to its high-quality goods sold at affordable prices. Since 2019, it has been growing into an eastern landmark cultural tourism market, concurrent with the development of the Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest.

title: Gwangjang Market
summary: Gwangjang Market is one of Korea's largest traditional markets and is renowned for its quality silk goods, linen bedding and hand-made goods.
overview:
As one of the most vibrant traditional markets in Seoul, Gwangjang Market is based in the center of the city so it can easily be located by even first-time visitors. This historic market opened in the early 20th century and is home to a number of clothing and food stalls, offering tourists a taste of traditional Korean cuisine. Starting with "addictive gimbap," one of Koreans’ all-time favorite snacks, and nokdujeon (mung bean pancake), visitors can sample a range of Korean delicacies. Other traditional treats such as tteok-bokki (stir-fried rice cake) and eomuk (fish cake) are also available. It is worth visiting the food stalls since most dishes are reasonably priced. If you have a keen interest in clothing, we recommend that you visit the hanbok stores and vintage clothing shops on the 2nd floor.

title: Gyeongdong Market
summary: A representative market of Seoul in Cheongnyangni where tradition and modernity harmonize
overview:
Gyeongdong Market is one of Seoul’s iconic traditional markets, located in Cheongnyangni, where tradition and modernity coexist. It is a vibrant cultural hub offering a wide range of goods including agricultural products, medicinal herbs, and seafood, and is a favorite destination among foreign tourists.
Established in June 1960 as a market specializing in agricultural goods, it has grown into a central traditional market in Seoul, offering a variety of mountain-harvested specialties and produce at reasonable prices. In 1985, with the completion of the Gyeongdong Building, the market expanded to become home to Korea’s largest ginseng and herbal medicine specialty zone, surpassing even Daegu Yakryeongsi in expertise and scale.

title: Hongdae R3 Fashion Street
summary: The hub of fashion and shopping in Hongdae
overview: The R3 area is a central spot for fashion and shopping, densely packed with a variety of clothing and cosmetic stores. With many stores popular on social media located here, the area enjoys great popularity among young people and tourists.

title: Hwanghak-dong Flea Market
summary: A market where old memories are piled up layer by layer.
overview: The Hwanghak-dong Flea Market started as a 'Dokkaebi Market' (Goblin Market) where people who lost their homes after the Korean War sold goods flowing out of US military bases. As time passed, it grew beyond simple secondhand goods trading into a 'Flea Market' encompassing scrap metal, antiques, and even discontinued household items. You can freely enter the antique shops with old signboards without having to buy anything.

title: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street
summary: The first place in Korea to sell antique furniture.
overview: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street is the first place in Korea to sell antique furniture. Back in the 60s, American soldiers would put out their furniture and sell them on the street before they headed back home to the US, leading to the formation of Itaewon Antique Furniture Street. At the present, there's close to 100 stores selling and renting out vintage and antique furniture. After Chungmuro, it's the next most frequented place by people working in the film and advertising industry. Hosting an "Itaewon Antique Festival" every October and "Weekend Flea Market" every weekend, this street is always attracting new visitors. It's a must-visit place for those interested in walking through a medieval European-like street in Seoul.

title: Jeil Market
summary: First opened in 1970, Jeil Market is made up of about 70 stores specializing in selling clothes, household products, side dishes, and food.
overview: First opened in 1970, Jeil Market is made up of about 70 stores specializing in selling clothes, household products, side dishes, and food. Around 10 bunsik (snack) stores can be found inside the market selling their famous flat dumplings and sundae (bloodsausages).

title: Jeungsan Market
summary: Jeungsan Market is made up of 180 stores including hardware stores, restaurants, and stores selling fresh produce, dairy, and fish.
overview: Jeungsan Market is made up of 180 stores including hardware stores, restaurants, and stores selling fresh produce, dairy, and fish. Famous for their 30 year old sundaeguk (blood sausage), this market houses about 10 different stores dedicated to this dishin its central area. In 2017, several youth projects were selected for a “Residents Participatory Budgeting Project," which led to opening up stores such as “Flower Tea Love Potion” and “Brothers’ Bar”, bringing back a renewed vitality to the market’s atmosphere.

title: Mangwon Market
summary: Mangwon Market is a traditional market in Seoul
overview: Mangwon Market, which has been around for over 40 years, is a traditional market in Seoul where visitors can fill their stomachs with delicious food at a low price. Visitors at the market should seek out Q's Dakgangjeong, which sells various kinds of chicken gangjeong, including spicy chicken gangjeong and fruit dakgangjeong, as well as Hwanginho Croquette, which sells spicy croquettes and donuts, which are famous at Mangwon Market. In addition to these options, there are many food items that are unique to Mangwon Market such as various snacks, tteokgalbi, and traditional alcohol. There are many restaurants to choose from, so it has become known as a hot spot in Mangwon-dong, which is commonly visited by many people in their 20s and 30s. Mangwon Hangang Park is also nearby, so it's recommended to pack delicious food from the market and then enjoy a picnic in the park. A paradise of cheap and varied food! Let's visit Mangwon Market.

title: Namdaemun Flower Market
address: 3rd Floor, E-World, 21 Namdaemun Market 4-gil, Jung-gu, Seoul
summary: The oldest flower market in Seoul that has continued its long history and tradition for over 40 years.
overview: Located inside Namdaemun Market, the Namdaemun Flower Market is the oldest flower market in Seoul. Continuing its long history and tradition for over 40 years, it is one of the four major flower markets in Seoul that supplies affordable and high-quality products to wholesale and retail customers from all over the country. You can feel the atmosphere of both a flower market and a traditional market together. Since it sells a variety of flower-related products, not only fresh flowers but also artificial flowers, dried flowers, flower baskets, ribbons, vases, interior props, and packaging materials, you can purchase fresh flowers, artificial flowers, and decorative props practically. Unlike other flower markets, it stays open relatively late, allowing visits even if it is not at dawn, and as it focuses mainly on retail sales, you can comfortably browse and purchase flowers.

title: Namdaemun Market
summary: Namdaemun Market is the largest traditional market in Korea with over 10,000 stores that line the streets around Namdaemun (Gate), the main southern gate of the old city wall.
overview:
Namdaemun Market is the largest traditional market in Korea with over 10,000 stores that line the streets around Namdaemun (Gate), the main southern gate of the old city wall. Namdaemun Market first started under the reign of King Taejong (1367 – 1422, the third Joseon king) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392 – 1910), when the government built shops around Namdaemun and rented out the shops to traders. It boasts one of the largest distribution structures in Korea, providing local products, daily living essentials, food products, medical supplies and more to retailers and consumers across the country.

Due to the wholesale nature of the market, shoppers can comparison shop for the lowest prices on all sorts of goods. Namdaemun Market is also packed with interesting things to see and eat, making it a popular destination for both locals and international visitors alike. So whether you’re looking for traditional oriental medicine or imported drugs, traditional Korean food or imported snacks, hanbok attire or a Halloween costume, Namdaemun Market is the place to go.

Namdaemun Market is renowned for its vast size and the variety of goods it offers. With the exception of construction materials, the market sells nearly every item under the sun including clothing, food, living essentials, etc. So it comes as no surprise that Namdaemun Market is always bustling day and night. Retailers from all over the nation flock to the market at night and local consumers flock to the market during the day. Many tourists come during the day as well to experience the charm of a traditional Korean market. The market's success is largely due to its independent distribution system. Although the shops are small, most of them produce the goods they offer themselves, allowing for customers to purchase goods directly from the manufacturers at wholesale prices.

title: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
summary: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market is the best place in Seoul to get fresh seafood at competitive prices.
overview: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market (or Noryangjin Fish Market for short) is the best place in Seoul to get fresh seafood at competitive prices. The market is both a wholesale outlet, trading in daily catches that arrive from every possible location, and also a retail market, where the public can get seafood at very low prices. The market is easily reached since it is conveniently connected to the subway station. The market is the largest fish market in Seoul. There are many restaurants ready to slice any fish bought at the market into hoe (raw fish) for their customers. During lunch and supper times, the market is bustling with customers browsing for fresh seafood. Nearby restaurants are ready to slice the fish that customers buy directly from the market into hoe. The usual arrangement is that the customer pays the fishmonger for the fish and the restaurant owner for the side dishes, vegetables or sauces. Daily auctions also take place from 1 am to 4 am. Among merchants, competition is fierce to get the freshest seafood, and tourists as well as citizens of Seoul like to come down to see this unusual scene. It is great fun to see and taste a wide range of seafood at the market, and everything bought and sold here comes fresh from the ocean.

title: Seoul Central Market
summary: Seoul Central Market, one of the many traditional markets in Seoul, is one of the three largest markets in Korea since the Korean War.
overview: Seoul Central Market, one of the many traditional markets in Seoul, is one of the three largest markets in Korea since the Korean War. The market’s nostalgic alleys are filled with delicious options such as fresh seafood, banchan dishes, and snacks such as sweet breads.

title: Seoul Folk Flea Market
summary: Korea’s largest flea market. Shop owners sell the second-hand goods which they gathered with efforts from everywhere.
overview:
Seoul Folk Flea Market is the largest flea market in Korea. The market sells typical Korean items, everyday goods, souvenirs, traditional goods and traditional food, allowing visitors to enjoy shopping and eating all under one roof. These days, the market has become one of the city's main attractions among local people as well as overseas visitors. Seoul Folk Flea Market is filled with Korean traditional goods and foods that reflect the simpler lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market opened in April 2008 and is a place alive with typical Korean folk items, souvenirs, traditional food and everyday goods that reveal the lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market holds performances of "Pungmulpae" (pungmul band, traditional Korean percussion band) all year round. Regional specialties and traditional and modern crafts are also bought and sold here. In this two-story building, everyday miscellaneous goods, antiques and clothing are found on the first floor, and restaurants are situated on the second floor.

Seoul Folk Flea Market is divided into seven zones; red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet, the colors of rainbow. The red zone is a food court. The orange zone is for regional specialties such as squid from Ulleungdo Island, traditional crafts like crockery, and bits and bobs such as smoking pipes etc. The yellow zone deals with secondhand vintage goods, such as typewriters, telephones etc. The green zone is for antiques, such as traditional antique furniture and art. The blue zone sells fashion accessories and the indigo zone sells clothing, paintings, calligraphy, hanji (traditional handmade Korean paper) and so on. Finally, the violet zone displays and sells miscellaneous goods, electronics, tools etc. The market has many rare goods that cannot easily be found elsewhere.

title: Seoul Yangnyeong Market
summary: Seoul Yangnyeong Market is one of the most famous oriental medicine markets in Korea. The market slowly started to establish itself in the late 1960s when small medicinal herbs stores started opening one by one.
overview:
Seoul Yangnyeong Market is one of the most famous oriental medicine markets in Korea. The market slowly started to establish itself in the late 1960s when small medicinal herbs stores started opening one by one. Today, the market has grown to become the nation's largest oriental medicine market, and 70 percent of the oriental medicine traded in Korea goes through here. Because the market is able to minimize distribution costs, the medicinal herbs sold here cost around 30 percent cheaper than elsewhere.

When you enter Seoul Yangnyeong Market, you are immediately struck by the unique fragrances of oriental medicine. All Korean medicinal herbs can be found here including several types of ginseng, dates, milk vetch roots, as well as a variety of herbal medicine preparations for maintaining good health. More than 800 oriental medicine shops and clinics are located in this area.

title: Shinheung Market

overview: Haebangchon Shinheung Market, which took on the name of Haebangchon Market after Korea's liberation in 1953, has been in operation for 70 years and has created a unique atmosphere for people of various nationalities and cultures to come together. There are various restaurants and unique cafes not only inside the market, but also outside the market. Visitors can find chicken, sushi restaurants, Thai food, noodles, and American fusion Chinese restaurants.It is a place with lots to see and to eat!

title: The store from Tong-in

overview: The oldest gallery specializing in antique art in Insadong, it was founded in 1924 as an antique art store representing Korea and became the backbone of culture and art during the turbulent times. The Tongin Gallery is located inside the Tongin Store and has become the center of Insadong as a complex cultural art space where ancient and contemporary art coexist. It is famous for its ancient art representing Korea and is a favorite place for world leaders. The tiger from a familiar folk tale is the representative character of Tongin Gallery.
